integrity: The proof reduces every fixed-firm positive profile to an integer partition of excess units. Herfindahl ordering becomes exact comparison of a quadratic integer sum, while entropy ordering becomes exact comparison of an integer product. Every partition through the sharp excess boundary is exhaustively checked, and the unique first reversing pair is reconstructed for arbitrary firm count.
scientific_limitations: The theorem fixes the number of firms and uses strictly positive integer market units on a common grid. It is an ordinal comparison of two concentration indices, not a claim about welfare, merger legality, or causal market power. Hart's 1971 article was available only through journal summary metadata in the checked routes, so the exact-date anchor is the first-published date of the later direct Herfindahl–entropy comparison by Acar and Sankaran.
title: Seven excess market units are the sharp HHI–entropy reversal boundary
